sec:mass-predictions-intro:
With the energy unit m_e (\mathrm{CAL\text{-}1}) and the aether modulus q_0 (\mathrm{CAL\text{-}2}) fixed from the lepton sector, the six-term categorical mass formula generates parameter-free predictions across the hadron and nuclear chart.

This section evaluates the stability cubic bounding the nuclear valley of stability up to Z = 103, states the conjecture that the curve of equal-energy neighbours is an elliptic curve isogenous to Bring's colour fibre, compares the predicted neutron number and local q-sensitivity intervals against AME 2020, and tabulates the resulting mass ratios and full three-channel Hecke atomic masses (Z \le 10) against CODATA 2022 and PDG 2024 benchmarks.
prop:neutron-prediction-comparison:
Proposition Comparison of predicted and observed stable neutron numbers for p \leq 103. At q = q_0, the beta-stability formula (beta-stability) fixes the beta-stability line p^*(A), the minimum-energy proton count at each mass number:

  p^*(A) =  \frac{A}{2 + c \cdot A^{2/3}},
  \qquad c = \frac{\lambda_C}{2a_{\mathrm{asym}}} = \frac{(q_0 - q_0^{-1})\,[6]_{q_0}}{6\,[2]_{q_0}[7]_{q_0}} \approx 0.01452,

with \lambda_C = (q - q^{-1})[6]_q\, m_e and a_{\mathrm{asym}} = 3[2]_q[7]_q\, m_e in balanced quantum integers, evaluated at the proton-pinned modulus q_0; the factor m_e cancels. The constant c is fixed by the q-integer coefficient assignments of Ch 11 §8, not derived: those assignments are stated, and nothing here derives the choice of [6]_q or 3[2]_q[7]_q.

The predicted neutron number at a given proton count is obtained by inverting that line: n_{\mathrm{pred}}(p) = A^*(p) - p, where A^* is the fixed point of A^* = p\left(2 + c\,{A^*}^{2/3}\right), rounded to the nearest integer. Compare n_{\mathrm{pred}} with the observed neutron number n_{\mathrm{obs}}(p) across 103 elements, where n_{\mathrm{obs}}(p) is the neutron number of the most abundant naturally occurring isotope (NUBASE2020), or of the longest-lived ground state for an element with no naturally occurring isotope:

The mean discrepancy is \overline{|\Delta n|} \approx 1.82. The maximum discrepancy |\Delta n| = 7 occurs at p = 52 (tellurium, whose most abundant isotope {}^{130}\mathrm{Te} lies far on the neutron-rich side).
rem:elliptic-stability-locus:
Remark The nuclear degeneracy locus is an elliptic curve over the Bring's surface. The stability curve and the color fibration of Bring's surface share the same algebraic origin. The conjecture is that the nuclear degeneracy locus — the curve in the (p, A)-plane where adjacent nuclei have equal energy — forms an elliptic curve isogenous to the fibrewise color curve \mathcal{E}_z.

The two cubics.

The color elliptic curve (color elliptic) at spacetime ratio z is:

  X^3 + (z + 1)X^2 + (z^2 + z + 1)X
  + (z^3 + z^2 + z + 1) = 0.
  \tag{C}

The nuclear stability condition (beta-stability), under the substitution t = A^{1/3}, yields:

  t^3 - cpt^2 - 2p = 0,
  \qquad c = \frac{a_C}{2a_A}
  = \frac{\lambda_C}{2a_{\mathrm{asym}}}.
  \tag{S}

Both are cubics in one variable parametrized by another. The color cubic (C) carries parameter z (spacetime) and variable X (color coordinate); the stability cubic (S) uses parameter p (Coulomb charge) and variable t (cube root of mass number).

Genus comparison.

The stability cubic (S) is rational. Solving for p yields p = t^3 / (2 + ct^2), confirming genus 0. The color cubic (C), as a curve in the (X,z)-plane, has genus 1: its projective closure is the smooth plane cubic \mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{col}} of color elliptic. For fixed z it is three points, and the fibrewise curve \mathcal{E}_z\colon y^2=F(X,z) is elliptic, with j-invariant a rational function of z.

The physical stability problem incorporates the pairing energy \pm \lambda_P / t^{3/2}, distinguishing even-even, even-odd, odd-even, and odd-odd nuclei. The degeneracy locus is the set of (p, t) at which an even-even nucleus (p, A) and the odd-odd nucleus (p+1, A) have equal energy. With the p-dependent energy a_C p^2/A^{1/3} + a_A (A-2p)^2/A of integer stability and pairing -\lambda_P/A^{1/2} (even-even) and +\lambda_P/A^{1/2} (odd-odd), the condition E(p+1) - E(p) = -2\lambda_P/A^{1/2}, multiplied by A/(4a_A) and written in t and \bar p = p + \tfrac12, is:

  t^3 - c\bar p\,t^2 - 2\bar p
  =  \frac{\lambda_P}{2a_A} \cdot t^{3/2}.
  \tag{D}

Squaring to clear the half-integer exponent and substituting u = t^{1/2} (so t = u^2, t^{3/2} = u^3, t^3 = u^6) gives:

  \bigl(u^6 - c\bar p\,u^4 - 2\bar p\bigr)^2
  =  \frac{\lambda_P^2}{4a_A^2} \cdot u^6.
  \tag{D$'$}

This defines a degree-12 curve in (\bar p, u). Factoring out the genus-0 component (the pairing-free stability curve) leaves a degree-6 residual curve in (p, u), generically of genus 1.

Conjecture. Let \mathcal{D} \subset \mathbb{A}^2 be the degeneracy locus (D') reduced by the pairing-free stability curve (S). Then:

  1. The smooth model of \mathcal{D} forms an elliptic curve \mathcal{E}_p over \mathbb{Q}(q).
  2. There exists an isogeny \varphi \colon \mathcal{E}_p \to \mathcal{E}_{z(p)} to the fibrewise color curve of Bring's surface, where z(p) is the spacetime ratio at which the quadratic coefficient of the color elliptic cubic (C) equals that of the stability cubic (S) under X = t:
  z(p) =  -(cp + 1).
  1. The integer points (p, A) \in \mathcal{E}_p(\mathbb{Z}) correspond to the stability pairs: the mass numbers A at which the even-even/odd-odd degeneracy falls exactly on an integer lattice point.

Coefficient matching.

The stability cubic, written as a monic cubic in t with parameter p, is

  t^3 - cp \cdot t^2 + 0 \cdot t - 2p = 0.

At z = -(cp+1) the color cubic (C) becomes, with z + 1 = -cp, z^2 + z + 1 = c^2p^2 + cp + 1 and z^3 + z^2 + z + 1 = (z+1)(z^2+1):

  X^3 - cp\,X^2 + \bigl(c^2p^2 + cp + 1\bigr) X
  - cp\bigl(c^2p^2 + 2cp + 2\bigr) = 0.

Identifying X = t, the coefficients compare as follows:

Coefficient Color (C) at z = -(cp+1) Stability (S) Agreement
X^2 -cp -cp for every p (defines z(p))
X^1 c^2p^2 + cp + 1 0 never for real cp (discriminant -3)
X^0 -cp(c^2p^2 + 2cp + 2) -2p only on c^3p^2 + 2c^2p + 2c = 2

The constant-term condition c^3p^2 + 2c^2p + 2c = 2 has, at c = \lambda_C/(2a_{\mathrm{asym}}) \approx 0.0145158337 (the asymmetry constant of neutron prediction comparison), the positive root p \approx 736.8, far beyond the heaviest known element (Z = 118). The linear coefficient never agrees. So under X = t the two cubics share only their quadratic coefficient.

Affine obstruction. No other identification does better. Removing the quadratic term writes a monic cubic as Y^3 + PY + Q, and a change of variable X \mapsto \alpha X + \beta with \alpha, \beta \in \mathbb{C}, \alpha \neq 0, sends (P, Q) \mapsto (\alpha^2 P, \alpha^3 Q). Hence

  J = \frac{4P^3}{4P^3 + 27Q^2}

is unchanged, and two cubics related by such a substitution have equal J. For (C),

  P_C = \frac{2z^2 + z + 2}{3}, \qquad
  Q_C = \frac{5(z+1)(4z^2 - z + 4)}{27},

and 2z^2 + z + 2 > 0 for real z, so P_C > 0 and 4P_C^3 + 27Q_C^2 > 0, giving J_C > 0. For (S),

  P_S = -\frac{c^2p^2}{3}, \qquad
  4P_S^3 + 27Q_S^2 = \frac{4p^2(54c^3p^2 + 729)}{27},

so J_S < 0 whenever c > 0 and p \neq 0. Therefore no substitution X \mapsto \alpha X + \beta carries (S) to (C) at any real z; equality of J requires complex z. Matching "up to a Möbius transformation" would add nothing, since any three distinct points of \mathbb{P}^1 map to any other three. The isogeny in item 2 is therefore the whole content of that item. This obstruction is proved.

Physical interpretation.

If the conjecture holds:

  • The three color tubes (r, g, b) of the color fibration correspond to the three sectors of nuclear binding: volume (strong), Coulomb (electromagnetic), and Pauli (exclusion).
  • The fibrewise elliptic curve \mathcal{E}_z at spacetime z encodes the allowed baryon configurations at that point; the stability elliptic curve \mathcal{E}_p at proton number p encodes the allowed nuclear configurations at that proton count.
  • The isogeny \varphi connects them, representing the passage from single-baryon color structure to multi-baryon nuclear structure — the same passage that takes the proton (proton) from a color-linked triple to a nucleus (stable nucleus).
  • The stability pairs act as the integer points of \mathcal{E}_p — the (p, A) \in \mathcal{E}_p(\mathbb{Z}) where the even-even/odd-odd degeneracy falls on a lattice point.

Computational evidence.

The fibrewise color curve \mathcal{E}_z at z = s - s^{-1}, s = \sqrt{q_0} (Descartes elliptic curve), is:

  \mathcal{E}_q  :  y^2 = x^3 + 0.7087x + 0.8056,
  \qquad \Delta = -16(4a^3 + 27b^2) \approx -303.17, \quad j \approx 129.86,

with a \approx 0.7087 and b \approx 0.8056 its Weierstrass coefficients. Since \Delta < 0, the real locus \mathcal{E}_q(\mathbb{R}) possesses a single connected component.

Stable hadrons as lattice points on the stability cubic.

The stable nuclei provide the \mathbb{N}^2 lattice points (Q, N) on the genus-0 stability cubic (Diophantine valley):

  t^3 =  p(2 + ct^2),
  \qquad A = Z + N = t^3.

This curve is rational: p = t^3/(2 + ct^2). For each mass number A \in \mathbb{N}, the stable proton number p serves as the exact integer minimiser of the convex quadratic E(p, A) (integer stability). There is no approximation — the integer minimiser of a convex quadratic is determined exactly.

Pairing lift to genus 1 (open).

The genus-0 stability cubic accounts for all stable nuclei via lattice-point enumeration. Whether the pairing energy lifts this curve to the genus-1 elliptic curve \mathcal{E}_q — and whether the stability pairs \{2, 8, 20, 28, 50, 82, 126\} then acquire an interpretation as integer points of \mathcal{E}_p — remains an open question. The structural parallel between the stability cubic and the color cubic (identical algebraic origin in the Bring's surface) is unproven, and the coefficient matching above agrees in the quadratic coefficient only, with the constant term agreeing at p \approx 736.8, outside the nuclear chart.

Established results:

  • The stable nuclei represent lattice points on the stability cubic (exact, from the Skein binding Lagrangian).
  • The Descartes elliptic curve \mathcal{E}_q exists and carries the stated invariants (exact, from the color fibration).
  • Under X = t at z = -(cp+1), the color cubic and the stability cubic share their quadratic coefficient; their linear coefficients never agree (exact, by the table above).
  • No substitution X \mapsto \alpha X + \beta carries (S) to (C) at real z, since J_C > 0 > J_S (proved).
  • The golden ratio degeneration at q = 1/\varphi^2 holds (exact, from the (s^2 + s - 1) factor).

The full numerical computation is carried out at 100-digit precision.

where \alpha = m_e \times 8G is the binding scale and \Phi is the quantum dilogarithm volume.

The volumes are the traced-volume closed forms evaluated at the canonical Markov parameter z = q^3/(q^2+1) = 0.6126880371 at q_0, pairing each strand with every later strand. Normalising a residual by it therefore divides a binding-scale error by a nucleon-scale mass, and the ratio is small for that reason rather than because the prediction is close.
